summary: Bahrain admits GCC citizens freely, and offers visas on arrival and eVisas to a broad list of nationalities including the EU, US, UK and much of Asia and Latin America; everyone else needs a visit visa arranged through a sponsor in Bahrain via the NPRA before travel, unless they hold a valid UAE, UK, US, Saudi or Schengen visa or a US Green Card, which opens the eVisa and the visa on arrival to them.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Bahrain?
faq.answer: GCC citizens enter freely with a national ID. A broad list of nationalities — including the EU, UK, US, Canada, Australia and much of Asia and Latin America — can get a visa on arrival or apply online for an eVisa. Nationalities outside those lists need a visit visa arranged through a sponsor in Bahrain (a hotel, company or relative) via the NPRA before travel. Holders of a valid visit visa for the UAE, UK, US or Saudi Arabia, a Schengen visa or a US Green Card can use the eVisa or the visa on arrival whatever their nationality.

faq.question: Should I get the Bahrain eVisa or a visa on arrival?
faq.answer: If you are eligible for both, the visa on arrival needs no application in advance: it is issued at Bahrain International Airport or the King Fahd Causeway, and the passport officer may ask for a confirmed return ticket. The eVisa (evisa.gov.bh) is applied for before travel and NPRA also offers longer and multiple-entry eVisas; some nationalities are eligible only for the eVisa.

faq.question: I live in Saudi Arabia / the UAE — can I get a visa on arrival?
faq.answer: NPRA offers residents of GCC states, whatever their nationality, a two-week single-entry eVisa applied for online from outside Bahrain, with the GCC residence permit attached and a return visa valid for at least 3 months; issuance takes one working day.

faq.question: Can Israeli citizens visit Bahrain?
faq.answer: Israeli passport holders can apply online for the Bahrain eVisa on evisa.gov.bh before travel; accommodation details and a return ticket are required.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Bahrain?
faq.answer: NPRA says the two-week eVisa can be extended by 14 days for BHD 25 at an NPRA service centre, and that guarantor-sponsored visit visas can be extended (BHD 30, one working day).
